title: Chat Application
summary: One-to-one and group messaging with presence and history.
problem: Design a chat service like WhatsApp or Slack: one-to-one and group conversations, delivery receipts, online presence, and message history.
functional: Send and receive messages in real time in 1:1 and group chats (up to 500 members)
Show sent, delivered and read states
Keep history and sync it across a user's devices
nonFunctional: Messages in a conversation arrive in order and are never lost
Message delivery under 200 ms for online users
constraints: Mobile clients disconnect and reconnect constantly
deliverables: Requirements and the assumptions you made
A capacity estimate (requests per second, storage, bandwidth)
A high-level architecture diagram (Mermaid or an uploaded image)
The API (endpoints and payloads) and the data model
How it scales, how it fails, and what you would monitor
The main trade-offs and what you chose not to build
hints: What protocol keeps a connection open to the client?
How do you order messages within a conversation across servers?
reference:
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C1[Client A] <-->|WebSocket| G1[Gateway 1]
  C2[Client B] <-->|WebSocket| G2[Gateway 2]
  G1 --> CS[Chat service]
  G2 --> CS
  CS --> MQ[[Message log per conversation]]
  MQ --> G2
  CS --> DB[(Message store, partitioned by conversation)]
  CS --> R[(Presence + routing: user to gateway)]
  CS --> PUSH[Push for offline users]
```

- Clients hold a **WebSocket** to a gateway; a routing table says which gateway a user is on, so the chat service can deliver to the right one.
- Each conversation is a **partition** with a sequence number, which gives the ordering guarantee; the message is persisted before it is acknowledged.
- Offline users get a **push** notification and fetch history by sequence number on reconnect, which is also how multi-device sync works.
- Presence uses heartbeats with a short TTL in a fast store; do not fan out presence to every contact, only to open chats.
- Large groups use fan-out on read for the message list and fan-out on write only for notifications.
